title: Would?
tuning: Eb Standard (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

rig.guitar: 1984 G&L Rampage "Blue Dress" (Seymour Duncan JB bridge humbucker)

amp.model: Bogner Fish preamp into VHT power amp (low layer of the three-amp Dirt split)

rig.notes: Contrary to a common assumption this is not drop D: transcriptions consistently give plain Eb standard, with the weight coming from the arrangement rather than a dropped sixth string. The Fish's Shark channel is the documented home of Cantrell's core rhythm voicing; aim for controlled rather than scooped bass so the chords keep note definition under the vocal. title: No Excuses

rig.notes: Eb standard, no capo - the capo 3 arrangements circulating online are transposed beginner versions, not what Cantrell played. The signature jangle comes from barre shapes moving against ringing open top strings, so set a bright, uncompressed clean and let the open strings bloom. title: Check My Brain
tuning: Drop C# / Drop Db (Db Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

rig.guitar: Gibson Les Paul Custom, or the G&L Rampage; Motor City bridge pickup

amp.model: Dave Friedman-built "Marsha" 50W Marshall-style head (Bogner Fish preamp also

pedals.model: Dunlop JC95 Jerry Cantrell Signature Cry Baby

settings.Threshold: Set just above the rig's noise floor

rig.notes: Transcriptions vary between drop D, drop C# and Eb standard, but the record sits in drop Db/C# - drop-D shapes moved down a half step. The lurching "seasick" character is fretting-hand, not a whammy bar: Cantrell described it as slightly out of tune, not quite a full bend, a two-note idea he credits to listening to Iommi.
